JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by her in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner is as follows:-
On 17-10-2022 at about 11-40 am., the petitioner as a pedestrian, was crossing road near Bakery, Thanisandra main road, Bangalore, at that time the rider of Two wheeler bearing No.KA-50-EE-3846 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner, result of which the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately the petitioner was shifted to Dr. B R Ambedkar Medical College and Hospital wherein admitted as an inpatient.

entities.text: B R Ambedkar Medical College and Hospital
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: So far, the petitioner has spent more than Rs.1,00,000/- towards medical and other expenses.
3. Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy.
Due to permanent disability, she had to depend on others for her day to day activities.
She has suffered pain and sufferings, permanent disability and other pecuniary and non-pecuniary damages.
4. In spite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 has remained absent.
Hence he was placed ex-parte.
5. Respondent no.2/

the Insurer of Two wheeler bearing No.KA-50-EE-3846 has filed written statement and admitted the coverage of insurance policy and the liability if any subject to the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.

The respondent no.2 has contended that insured vehicle was not involved in the accident, that the petitioner in collusion with the jurisdictional police and the owner of the vehicle has fixed the vehicle for unlawful gain and that the driver of the Insured car was not holding valid and effective driving license.

6. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that, she has sustained injuries on account of Road Traffic Accident on 17-10-2022 at about 11-40 am., near R K Bakery, Thanisandra Kadle Rangamma vs Manjunath on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138942118/
2 main road, Bangalore, due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-50-EE-3846?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, what is the quantum?
From whom?
3. What Order or Award?
7.
The petitioner got examined herself as Pw1 and one witness is examined as P.W.2 and got marked documents as per Ex.P1 to Ex.P6.

The respondent No.2 has examined its Legal Manager as RW.1 and got marked documents as per Ex.R1 and Ex.R2.
8.
Heard arguments of learned counsel for the petitioner and respondent no.2 and perused the entire materials placed on record.

9. My findings on the above issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1: In the Affirmative  Issue No.2: Partly in the affirmative.
Issue No.3:
Issue No.1:-

In order to explain the actionable negligence of the rider of Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA- 50-EE-3846 , the P.W.1 has filed affidavit explaining the vivid picture of the accident that took place on 17-10- 2022 at about 11-40 am., when the petitioner as a pedestrian, was crossing road near Bakery, Thanisandra main road, Bangalore, at that time the rider of Two wheeler bearing No.KA-50-EE-3846 (herein after called the offending vehicle) came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner, result of which she fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

P.W.1 further deposed about the nature of injuries sustained, treatment taken and the amount spent for treatment etc.
11.

In support of the claim and to prove the rash and negligent riding of the offending vehicle, P.W.1 has relied upon Ex.P1, P2, P4 and P5 which are the police records such as FIR with complaint,
wound certificate, order sheet in CC No.476/2023 and charge sheet, etc.,
12.

On the basis of the complaint lodged by the petitioner, case has been registered against the rider of offending vehicle in Crime No.0174/2022 by Chikkajala Traffic Police Station for the offence punishable under section 279 and 337 of IPC.
After completion of investigation, the Investigation officer has filed charge sheet against the rider of offending vehicle for the offence punishable under Section 279 and 338 of IMV act.

13. The learned counsel for respondent no.2 has submitted that the petitioner has not proved the Kadle Rangamma vs Manjunath on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138942118/
3 involvement of offending vehicle in the accident and that except producing FIR and wound certificate, the petitioner has not produced any other document.
14.

In the light of the argument canvassed by the learned counsel for petitioner, if the evidence of the petitioner is perused, she has produced FIR with complaint, wound certificate, medical bills, order sheet in CC No.476/2023 and entire charge sheet which contains spot mahazar, sketch, notice u/Sec. 133 MV Act, reply and other related documents.
It appears that learned counsel for respondent no.2 has not gone through the evidence of petitioner and lost sight of the documents produced by the petitioner.

15. If the MLC and Police intimation produced by the petitioner which is the part and parcel of charge sheet is perused, soon after the accident the petitioner has taken treatment at Dr.
B.R.Ambedkar Medical College and Hospital on the history of RTA on 17-10- 2022 at around 11-40 am., near Thanisandra, R.K Bakery by two wheeler bearing No.KA-50-EE-3846.

entities.text:
Dr.
B.R.Ambedkar Medical College and Hospital
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: From the said document it can very well be said that the offending vehicle was involved in the accident.
16. If the spot mahazar and sketch is perused, at the time of accident the petitioner was crossing the road near R.K Bakery.
It is two way road.
The width of the road at the spot of accident is nearly 60 feet.
The offending vehicle was proceeding from Thanisandra and hit to the petitioner who was crossing the road.

There is no any evidence placed by the respondent no.2 to say that there was zebra crossing nearby the spot of accident and the petitioner without using the zebra crossing has crossed the road in some other place.
When offending vehicle was proceeding from Thanisandra he ought to have drive the vehicle on the left side of the said road.

But if the sketch is perused, the petitioner has almost crossed the road and when she is about to reach the other end of the road, the offending vehicle by coming from Thanisandra on the extreme right side of the road hit to the petitioner.
Hence, from the spot mahazar and sketch it can be said that the accident in question has occurred due to the sole negligence on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle.

Since, the rider of the offending vehicle is the cause for the accident, in the criminal case registered against him in CC No. 476/2023, on service of summons he appeared before the court and pleaded guilty and deposited the fine amount.
Hence, without discussion much on this point, this court holds above point in the Affirmative.
17. Issue No.2:- The petitioner has given evidence to the effect of her sustained injures all over her body.

Ex.P2 is the wound certificate issued from DR. B R Ambedkar Medical College and Hospital to the effect that the petitioner has taken primary treatment and has been treated for two injuries which are grievous in nature.

entities.text: B R Ambedkar Medical College and Hospital
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 18. The petitioner has stated that she has taken treatment at Dr. B R Ambedkar Medical College and Hospital at Bangalore, wherein she was admitted as an inpatient.

entities.text: B R Ambedkar Medical College and Hospital at Bangalore
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: But the petitioner has not produced discharge summary to let the court know the period of treatment taken by the petitioner as an inpatient.
19. Dr. Jayashri - working at Dr. B R Ambedkar Medical College is examined as PW.2.

As per the evidence of PW.2, petitioner has taken treatment as outpatient and x-ray was taken and it was Kadle Rangamma vs Manjunath on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138942118/
4 referred to orthopedician and confirmed that petitioner had fracture injuries.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 20. The petitioner has not examined the medical officer who has given treatment to her and there is no evidence on record to say that petitioner has suffered permanent disability.
As such there is no loss of future income.
Hence, petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head of loss of future income.
21. Towards pain and sufferings, the petitioner shown to have sustained two grievous injuries.

Hence taking into consideration the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, time taken for treatment and sufferings during the treatment etc, it is reasonable to hold that petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.70,000/- towards pain and suffering.
22. So far as the medical expenses incurred by the petitioner are concerned, she has produced 33 medical bills for Rs.60,336/- as per Ex.P3.

Hence, petitioner is entitled for compensation under the head medical expenses to the tune of Rs.60,336/-.
23.
It is stated that petitioner was aged about 61 years.
She was a house wife.

Hence this court considering the age of petitioner, year of accident and place of residence of the petitioner, taken the income of the petitioner at Rs.15,500/- p.m.
24.
The petitioner has sustained two grievous injuries and has taken treatment as inpatient at Dr. B R Ambedkar Medical college & Hospital as per Medical bills.

entities.text: B R Ambedkar Medical college & Hospital
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Hence the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, which are grievous in nature it is reasonable to hold that period of 3 months as complete laid down period.

Hence taking into consideration the states of the petitioner as house wife and her contribution to the family, this court takes the loss of income during laid down period as Rs.15,500/- p.m. for three month.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.46,500/-
towards loss of income during the laid down period .
25. From the evidence of Pw1 and as borne out by medical bills, petitioner has taken treatment Dr. B R Ambedkar Medical college & Hospital.

entities.text: B R Ambedkar Medical college & Hospital
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Further for taking treatment in the said hospital she was to travel to the hospital for treatment.
She has taken nourishment and needs further nourishment at this age and incurred other incidental expenses.
Therefore all together incidental expenses is assessed at Rs.10,000/- taking in to consideration the cost of living and value of the money during the year 2024.
26. The petitioner at her age of 61 years has suffered grievous injuries which definitely would cause some amount of discomfort and loss of amenities in life.
Hence, petitioner is entitled for compensation under the head loss of amenities and discomfort to the tune of Rs.60,000/-.

Thus the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
 Sl. Heads Amount  No.
 1. Towards pain and sufferings Rs. 70,000/-
 2.

Medical expenses Rs. 60,336/-
 3. Towards Conveyance, Attendant Rs. 10,000/-

5  charges and nourishing food  & other incidental charges

 laid up period  5. Loss of discomfort and amenities Rs. 60,000/-
Total Rs

Therefore this court holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.2,46,836/- (Rupees Two Lakh Forty Six Thousand Eight Hundred Thirty Six only).
27.
As regarding liability is concerned, there is no dispute that offending vehicle was insured with 2nd respondent and policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Further the driver of the offending vehicle had driving license to drive the offending vehicle.
Hence it can be said that all the documents pertaining to the vehicle in question was valid and in force as on the date of accident.

Hence by fastening liability on the respondent No.2 this Tribunal directs the respondent no.2 to pay compensation to the petitioner along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of payment of entire amount.
Accordingly Issue No. 2 is answered.
28. Issue No.3:
In the light of findings given on Issue No.1 and 2, my finding on this issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioner is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.2,46,836/- + cost of Rs.1,000/- imposed vide order on IA No.III.
Thus, the petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.2,47,836/- (Rupees Two Lakh Forty Seven Thousand Eight Hundred Thirty Six only).
A Sum of Rs.2,46,836/- shall also carry interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The Respondent No.2 is liable to pay compensation and is directed to deposit the compensation along with interest within two months from the date of award.
On deposit entire amount and interest is ordered to be released in favour of the petitioner on proper identification.
Advocates' fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the stenographer directly on computer, corrected and then pronounced by me in open court, on this the 6th day of January 2026.)
(ROOPASHRI) XXII Addl. SCJ & ACJM Bengaluru.
